svg.text: Turning a setback into a shared opportunity
A resilient group can turn an unexpected problem into an opportunity by being resourceful
Our community film night lost its usual venue, so we had to draw on our local contacts. I brought up the problem at a
meeting and asked whether anyone had come across something worth watching. Not only did a neighbour suggest a
suitable film, but she also offered her garden as a screening space.
When she asked about equipment, I said, “Let me get back to you on that.” The ball was in my court, so I checked
what we could borrow before promising anything. The venue change proved a blessing in disguise: the smaller
Naming what matters and responding carefully can make a setback useful.
